chunks: Everything in this book that is narrated from Juhaim ibn Abi Juham has been transmitted by me from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan - may Allah be pleased with him - from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Saffar, from Al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Sa'd ibn Muslim, from Juhaim ibn Juham, who is also known as Ibn Abi Juhamah.

key_terms.الْعَبَّاسُ بْنُ مَعْرُوفٍ: Al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, a narrator in the chain.
key_terms.جُهَيْمُ بْنُ أَبِي جَهْمٍ: Juhaim ibn Abi Juham, a narrator whose transmissions are being clarified.
key_terms.رَوَيْتُهُ: I narrated it, indicating the author's direct transmission.
key_terms.سَعْدَانُ بْنُ مُسْلِمٍ: Sa'dan ibn Muslim, a narrator in the chain.
key_terms.مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْحَسَنِ: Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan, a key link in the transmission chain.
key_terms.مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْحَسَنِ الصَّفَّارُ: Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Saffar, a prominent scholar in the chain.

ai.seo_question: Who is the narrator Juhaim ibn Abi Juham and how is his narration transmitted in this book?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq provides a detailed biographical note to authenticate the narration of Juhaim ibn Abi Juham, clarifying his identity as the son of Abu Juham and tracing the chain through prominent Kufan scholars like Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad. This emphasis on the isnad reflects the Shia scholarly tradition's rigorous approach to verifying the reliability of narrators, particularly those from the era of the Imams, ensuring the hadith's integrity for legal and theological derivation.
